note: Fits the health criteria and misses both commercial ones. Neglected_health is textbook — no crisis, just a wrestler and powerlifter who stopped at 25 when corporate life and three young boys arrived, with the only clinical notes being a family cardiac history he has never acted on and a knee that flares when he runs. Good_to_great holds on his own framing: he explicitly says he is not embarrassed by his body and could walk around a pool today, he simply knows what he looked like when he trained. Not_deconditioned holds comfortably — he climbs roofs for a living, walks neighbourhoods door-knocking, walked 18 holes recently and did a full leg session the day before the call. Successful misses on the criterion as stated: it wants a business owner, physician or equivalent, and he is a salaried branch manager on a $75,000 base at a newly opened branch, not an owner. Income misses plainly and by his own account — 'the funds aren't there', a credit score around 630-680, a private school re-budget underway and a family relocation in the same month. This is the third prospect in this batch, after Bennu Kham Ra Ankh Aten and Kitch Cash, whose commercial profile sits outside the stated ICP, and the pattern across those three is worth carrying up: the ICP's occupation and income tests are not describing the people this rep is actually being booked with. Note also for the comparison the icp.json observations invite — where an off-ICP prospect got a discounted price on the Bennu call, this one asked directly for a lower number and was refused. Same misfit, different rep behaviour, on calls four days apart.
